parallel.requirements: The run recognized the ESM .mjs requirement, manual argparse-compatible CLI parsing, pure JavaScript AES-ECB behavior, Python bytes representation, local imports only, output in /output, and no node:crypto cipher APIs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent announced a split where one child would probe argparse behavior and another would validate AES output while the parent built the JS modules. The parent also retained de facto implementation and finalization ownership.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a nested module tree with lib/index.mjs, lib/cli/parser.mjs, lib/text/utf8.mjs, lib/format/python_bytes_repr.mjs, and lib/aes/*, while the aes_probe child later wrote a second flat module set plus a replacement /output/test15.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained both the parent nested modules and the child flat modules. The final response described the parent nested layout, but the shared entrypoint had been rewritten by a child during the run.
parallel.verification: The parent checked sample outputs, parser errors, one byte-for-byte comparison, and a standard AES-128 vector; it waited for children only near the end and did not consume a final child handoff.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Both children were still running when interrupted, no child final result reached the parent, and the official evaluator failed the final artifact with 6 of 29 tests passing.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual CLI, pure JS AES-ECB, Python bytes repr, local import, no external dependency, and no node:crypto requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the full pipeline: reference behavior probing, module design, implementation, parser and runtime-error refinement, randomized checks, and final response.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote lib/aes/field.mjs, tables.mjs, key_schedule.mjs, core.mjs, ecb.mjs, lib/cli/arg_parser.mjs, lib/python/bytes_repr.mjs, traceback.mjs, and /output/test15.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact used one coherent hierarchy and all writes and later traceback edits were made by the same actor before final delivery.
serial.verification: The serial run verified samples, parser edge cases, Unicode UTF-8 cases, and a 100-case randomized valid-input differential check, ending with all-checks-ok.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite stronger local verification, the completed official evaluation still failed at 6 of 29 tests; no allowed evaluator detail identifies the hidden mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task requirements from the same prompt and implemented against the same executable behavior.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept reference probing, implementation, verification, and closure in one actor with no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced concurrent probe ownership and shared workspace side effects; serial had a single owner for the whole pipeline.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent delegated probe work through encrypted child briefs and later the aes child wrote its own entrypoint and modules, showing no visible enforced file-ownership boundary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all interface decisions in one trajectory and therefore did not need cross-agent handoff or file ownership contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-actor coordination boundaries around probing and file ownership; serial avoided those boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented a nested library export structure, but a child later implemented a flat alternative with a different entrypoint dependency graph.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented one module tree and later modified the entrypoint to add Python-style traceback rendering.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ended with competing implementation paths in one artifact; serial evolved a single path in-place.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both children were still listed as running after parent waits, and the parent interrupted them before any final child result returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its own long-running randomized check completed with all-checks-ok before finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost delegated probe results at closure, while serial carried its verification result directly into the final decision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final artifact included both flat child modules and nested parent modules after two actors wrote the shared /output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and patched the same artifact tree in a single thread, with no cross-agent write collision.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a shared-state provenance problem centered on test15.mjs; serial had ordinary single-owner edits.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified samples, a byte-for-byte sample, parser cases, and an AES vector, but did not perform verification tied to a received child result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran samples, parser cases, Unicode tests, randomized valid cases, and a final all-checks-ok comparison pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had broader local verification and an explicit final aggregate check; parallel verified enough local cases to proceed but without integrating child handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent extra budget on two children, then waited twice, listed both children still running, interrupted them, and closed shortly afterward.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one longer single-thread run, completed its background command polling, and finalized after all-checks-ok.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure had unresolved child work; serial closure had no unresolved child tasks even though both official evaluations failed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed status records show no discordant outcome: both parallel and serial failed with 6 of 29 tests passing. The process difference is that parallel introduced child lifecycle loss and a shared entrypoint overwrite, while serial maintained one coherent actor-owned implementation path and broader local verification. Those differences are real parallel-side coordination issues, but the mounted evidence does not prove they explain a score gap because there is no score gap.
parallel_contributors: Parallel spawned two probe children and interrupted them while still running, so their final findings were unavailable at closure.
A child wrote a replacement required entrypoint and flat module tree after the parent had already written its own entrypoint and nested module tree.
serial_contributors: Serial kept probing, implementation, traceback adjustment, randomized testing, and final delivery inside one actor.
Serial completed an all-checks-ok verification pass before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The exact hidden evaluator mismatch is not exposed by the allowed files; both artifacts passed only 6 of 29 official samples despite local successful checks.
Serial added Python-style traceback frames after detecting an invalid-input mismatch; parallel only reported simpler ValueError behavior in its final verification notes.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official pass counts are mounted; no per-case failure log is available inside the allowed inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns are adverse parallel process issues rather than pass/fail causes

Investigation and implementation overlapped; the parent wrote modules before child investigations completed, so this was not a separate serial investigation phase.
No indispensable implementation path is shown starved by auxiliary work; the parent completed its implementation and checks before closure.
The run used only two spawned children and did not hit the cell timeout; the adverse events are explicit interruption and entrypoint overwrite, not fan-out exhaustion.
The children performed bounded probe work; there is no directly evidenced single overbroad child assignment whose unfinished scope displaced required work.
The child briefs are encrypted and the observable child actions show probing and implementation; no known task requirement is proven absent from a child brief and then followed into unusable work.
A missing file-ownership contract is plausible but not the most specific observed event; the concrete consequence is a child replacing the required entrypoint.
No known finding is shown present before a transfer and absent after transfer; the children did not provide final handoffs at all.

No incompatible child reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated; the conflict was a shared-file write, handled under Concurrent Writes.
The parent did perform integrated local checks and no parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap is shown before final; the later official failure alone cannot create this label.
